id_and_class.theory_title: James’s Radical Empiricism of Monistic Pure Experience
id_and_class.summary: William James argues that mind and matter are two ways of organizing one more basic field of ‘pure experience’, which is itself neither mental nor physical. The same bit of experience counts as a physical object in one set of relations and as someone’s perception in another, so consciousness names a function, not a substance.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a Function Within Pure Experience

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is pure experience taken in certain relations: retrospective, appropriative, personal, cognitive, practical and affective. The physical is the same experience taken in relations of stability, resistance, publicity and causal efficacy.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mind and body are two orderings of one stock of experience. James's example is a room, which belongs to a physical series with its own history and laws and also to a perceiver's biography, without being duplicated.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (pure experience is basic; the mental and the physical are relational roles it plays, not products that emerge from it)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Being ‘had’ by a subject is a relational fact about how experiences are grouped, not an extra ingredient. Knowing is a relation between portions of experience, so no transcendental ego is needed to connect knower and known.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Each bit of pure experience is made of whatever appears in it (space, intensity, flatness, brownness, heaviness). Qualities belong to experience itself and are counted as mental or physical depending on context.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Concrete portions of pure experience, and relations (conjunctive and disjunctive) that are themselves directly experienced. No soul, transcendental ego, or separate mental stuff.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through experience alone. Radical empiricism admits nothing that cannot be experienced at some point, and admits every experienceable thing, relations included.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Many qualitatively different bits of experience linked by experienced relations, which sort them into a personal mental series and a public physical series.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal experience, the subject-object distinction, knowing, and the mind-body problem itself.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Double counting: one portion of experience enters two relational contexts and so plays two roles. What makes an item mental is the company it keeps, not an intrinsic mark.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Experience is first given whole, before it is sorted into subject and object, inner and outer. The sorting happens as experiences are taken up into different chains of relations over time.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Not located in a head or inner medium. Consciousness is a pattern of relations among experiences that also make up the perceived world.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness performs the function of knowing. Causal efficacy belongs to the physical ordering of experience, one of the relational contexts experience can enter.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Relations are given in experience as directly as the things they relate, so the connective tissue of experience needs no synthesizing ego or external principle.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: James rejects the picture of an inner mind representing an outer world. A perceived room is the room, counted once in a physical series and once in a mental series.
core_claims_and_evidence: James holds that ‘consciousness’ names no entity or stuff, only a function performed within pure experience.
One bit of experience can belong to both a physical series and a mental series, so mind and matter differ only in their relations.
Radical empiricism treats relations as directly experienced, which removes the need for a transcendental ego to unify experience.
There is no single neutral stuff; each bit of experience is made of whatever qualities appear in it.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and phenomenological: analysis of what is given in experience, guided by an empiricist method.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Critics ask whether pure experience is genuinely neutral: if the basic stuff is ‘experience’, the view may be idealism in disguise. Others doubt that the two-orderings device explains phenomenal character, as opposed to relocating it. Contemporaries misread the 1904–05 essays and some psychologists took James to have abandoned psychology.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Because James denies a single general stuff, it is unclear whether ‘pure experience’ names a monism at all or a nominalist refusal to answer what experience is made of.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Internally consistent as a relational, contextual monism, and it dissolves the gulf between mind and matter rather than bridging it. Its pluralism of qualities sits uneasily with the claim to be a monism.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: In Human Immortality James proposed that the brain might transmit rather than produce consciousness, but he declined to claim the evidence settled the question of survival.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: The theory sets out a pluralistic, open universe with no single closed system, and does not by itself supply a cosmic purpose.
